title: Review B4a (T-0023) with security checklist: Scrapling fetch, RSC chunk parser, bench.json, cli bench, new dependency
spec: Adversarial review of the commit(s) on task/T-0023 (your worktree is based on that branch; verify `ls orchestrator/bench.py tests/fixtures` first). Apply skills/review/adversarial-review/references/security-checklist.md because this adds a network fetch and a third-party dependency. Focus: (1) no network access at import time or during tests (grep for Fetcher.get call sites; the fixture path must be used by tests); (2) parse_chunks: regex/JSON-unescape robustness on hostile input (catastrophic backtracking, huge chunks, nested quotes); never raises on a malformed chunk; bounded memory on a 1.4 MB page; (3) fetch(): the 20 h minimum interval is enforced from the file's fetched_at, --force bypasses it, and a fetch failure leaves the previous bench.json intact; (4) bench.json content is treated as data: nothing from the page is ever executed, eval'd, or used as a path or command; unmatched names are truncated; (5) the dependency: pyproject pins a version range, no [fetchers] browser extra, uv.lock consistent; check what scrapling itself pulls in and flag anything surprising; (6) User-Agent identifies the orchestrator if the API allows headers; (7) tests assert behaviour. Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` and report the result line. Return ONLY {"verdict":"approve|request_changes","comments":[...]} under 3,000 chars.
acceptance: security checklist applied and any finding cited by checklist item

comments.issue: Fetcher.get() never disables impersonate/stealthy_headers, so every fetch defaults to impersonate="chrome" + stealthy_headers=True (curl_cffi TLS/JA3 fingerprint spoofing, synthetic browser headers, fake Google referer) — the opposite of the file banner comment (lines 1-3) promising an identified, non-browser request. Contradicts the stated ToS-compliance rationale; is de-facto bot-detection evasion. [checklist #7 deps not used per stated justification]

http_status is a hardcoded literal 200, never read from Response.status. A blocked/rate-limited/CAPTCHA response (403/429/503) would still be recorded as a successful 200 fetch with empty/unmatched models, hiding fetch failures from provenance. [checklist #8 errors must fail closed, not silently report success]

match() requires exact (case-insensitive) equality between hint and name/slug, but the live site appends effort-variant suffixes (e.g. "GPT-6 Astra (max)"); DEFAULT_HINTS bare names will not exact-match, so real fetches will likely land almost everything in unmatched_names instead of models. (Branch later fixes this in e29a97e, confirming the gap is real.)
Test result: uv run python -m unittest tests.test_orchestrator -v -> Ran 59 tests, OK (all pass).
